name: Chromatic Prediction Error — How Architectural Color Confirms or Violates the Brain's Color Expectations
short_description: Color predictions arise from three converging sources: ecological associations (Palmer EVT), cultural-contextual meaning (Elliot), and regional architectural expectation (Lenclos); categorical color organization (Conway) structures PE magnitude; habituation reduces static color effects over days-weeks
structural_pattern: The brain generates color predictions for architectural contexts from THREE SOURCES operating simultaneously: (a) ECOLOGICAL ASSOCIATIONS (Palmer's EVT) — affective valence of objects associated with the color (blue → sky → positive; dark yellow → bile → negative); (b) CULTURAL-CONTEXTUAL MEANING (Elliot's Color-in-Context) — learned meaning of color in specific setting (red in restaurant → appetite; red in exam room → failure); (c) REGIONAL-ARCHITECTURAL EXPECTATION (Lenclos's geography of color) — color palette characteristic of local built environment (Mediterranean ochre, Scandinavian white, Japanese earth tones). These converge to generate composite chromatic prediction. Match = zero chromatic PE = comfort. Violation = PE that can be positive (delightful surprise) or negative (jarring conflict). CATEGORICAL STRUCTURE (Conway): Brain's categorical color organization means within-category changes produce minimal PE; between-category changes produce substantial PE. This structures color harmony: monochromatic = low PE = harmony; complementary = high PE = contrast. Goldilocks applies: moderate chromatic PE optimal. HABITUATION (Küller): Chromatic PE habituates over days-weeks with sustained exposure. Novel color → PE → prediction updates → PE drops to zero. Dynamic color maintains PE; static color habituates.
higher_order_principle: Architectural color is a prediction-violation phenomenon operating through three converging prediction sources (ecological, cultural-contextual, regional). Color effects are always context-dependent, always moderated by lighting, and always subject to habituation. The architect composes chromatic PE just as SC3 composes spatial PE: base palette sets arousal level for sustained occupancy, with controlled chromatic peaks at significant moments.

ecological_valence.mechanism: Colors preferred based on valence of associated objects

cultural_contextual.mechanism: Same color, different effects based on context meaning
cultural_contextual.examples: Red in restaurant = appetite; red in exam = failure anxiety

regional_expectation.mechanism: Regional palettes create place-specific color expectations
regional_expectation.examples: Mediterranean ochres; Scandinavian whites; Japanese earth tones

categorical_structure.within_category: Light blue → medium blue = minimal PE
categorical_structure.harmony_implication: Monochromatic/analogous = low PE; complementary = high PE

causal_links.evidence_base: Elliot & Maier (2012, ~1,500 citations) establish context-dependence. Palmer & Schloss (2010, ~700 citations) establish ecological association. Three-source convergence is template synthesis.
Conway et al. (2010, ~300 citations) establish categorical color organization. Franklin et al. (2005, ~400 citations) demonstrate categorical perception effects.
Küller et al. (2006, ~300 citations) document habituation of color effects in real rooms over days to weeks.

scope_conditions: Applies to all architectural surfaces with chromatic content — walls, ceilings, floors, furniture, fixtures
Color always perceived under illumination; predictions require specification of both surface color and light source
Digital displays (screens, LED panels) produce color through emission — different perceptual regime
Color blindness (~8% of males) alters prediction structure — dichromats have reduced categorical system
moderators: Lighting: same surface color appears different under warm, cool, and daylight illumination
Material texture: matte vs. glossy surfaces produce different color experiences from same pigment
Room size: immersive color produces stronger effects than accent color
Occupancy duration: sustained → habituation → reduced PE; transient → maintained PE
Individual color history: personal associations can override ecological and cultural defaults

interactions.nature: T1 addresses spatial frequency/fractal properties. COL1 addresses chromatic properties. Both contribute to visual processing of architectural surfaces through different channels.
T2's Goldilocks applies to chromatic PE: moderate chromatic complexity occupies optimal zone.
MAT5 formalizes cultural conditioning for materials. COL1's cultural-contextual source operates through same mechanism.
L1 addresses luminance contrast; COL1 addresses chromatic contrast. Color accent against neutral background produces both luminance PE (L1) and chromatic PE (COL1).
